title: Niobrara Mineral Rights
metaTitle: Sell Niobrara / DJ Basin Mineral Rights in Wyoming
metaDescription: The DJ Basin's Niobrara play crosses into Laramie and Goshen counties. If you hold minerals near Cheyenne or Torrington, get a written offer today.
heroLead: Most people talk about the Niobrara as a Colorado play, but it crosses the state line into Laramie and Goshen counties, and the mineral ownership up here is priced differently than it is south of the border.
intro: Cheyenne is the county seat of Laramie County, and Torrington is the county seat of Goshen County to the northeast. The DJ Basin's Niobrara chalk runs south from here into Colorado, but the northern edge of the play — the Silo Field near Cheyenne and acreage around Hawk Springs and Chugwater — has its own drilling history going back to the 1980s, well before the horizontal boom made the Niobrara a household name further south.

Because this is the flank of the play rather than the core, well results here vary more section to section than they do in the thickest part of the chalk down in Weld County, Colorado. That makes local production history, not only the play name on a map, the thing that actually sets what your minerals are worth.

sections.heading: Silo Field and the Older Vertical Wells
paragraphs: Silo Field, straddling the Wyoming-Colorado line in Laramie County, was one of the first places anyone drilled the Niobrara chalk specifically, with vertical wells going in during the late 1980s and early 1990s. A lot of those original wells are long since stripper production or plugged, but the field proved the chalk would produce here, and it's part of why operators came back decades later with horizontal technology aimed at the same rock.

If your family's minerals trace back to a lease from that earlier vertical era, the original lease terms and even the original well may still be relevant to your title, even though the economics of the play have completely changed since then. We look at both the old lease history and current activity nearby before pricing an interest like this.

sections.heading: The Railroad Checkerboard Reaches Cheyenne
paragraphs: Laramie County sits right on the original Union Pacific transcontinental line, which means the checkerboard pattern of alternating private railroad sections and federal sections runs directly through some of this acreage. It's the same 1862 Pacific Railway Act grant that checkerboards the Powder River Basin further north, just at the other end of the line. A section a few miles from Cheyenne can be entirely private minerals while the section next to it is federal, with no visible difference on the ground.

That matters here specifically because a horizontal Niobrara well can be permitted to drain both a private and a federal section in the same unit, which means your royalty deck might include both privately negotiated and federally set terms depending on exactly which section your minerals sit in. We verify that against county plat records before quoting a number.

sections.heading: Flank Position Changes the Math
paragraphs: The core of the Niobrara chalk thickens and gets more consistently productive as you move south into Colorado. Up here on the Wyoming side, the chalk is thinner in places and well results have more spread between a strong producer and a mediocre one. That doesn't mean your minerals are worth less on principle, but it does mean we weight nearby actual well performance more heavily than basin-wide averages when we evaluate a Laramie or Goshen County tract.

Goshen County, further from the historic Silo development, has seen less drilling overall, so acreage there is priced more on lease bonus and permitting trends than on an established royalty stream for most owners. If you're in Goshen County with undeveloped minerals, that's a normal position for this part of the play, not a sign your acreage is worthless.

sections.heading: Getting to a Number
paragraphs: We start with the Laramie or Goshen County clerk's deed and lease records to confirm what you actually own and whether it's inside the checkerboard's private or federal pattern. From there we look at any producing wells on or near your section, whether from the original Silo-era verticals or newer horizontal work, and current permitting activity in the area.

Send us your legal description, county, and any lease or division order paperwork you have, and we'll get back to you with a written offer, explained in plain terms, that reflects where exactly your minerals sit in this play.

faqs.question: Is the Wyoming Niobrara the same as the Colorado Niobrara?
faqs.answer: Same formation, different position in the play. The Colorado side around Weld County is the thick core; the Wyoming side around Laramie and Goshen counties is the northern flank, with thinner chalk and more variable well results.

faqs.question: What is Silo Field?
faqs.answer: Silo Field is an older Niobrara chalk field straddling the Laramie County, Wyoming and Weld County, Colorado line, first drilled with vertical wells in the late 1980s. It's one of the earliest proven Niobrara producing areas.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Laramie County section is checkerboard federal or private?
faqs.answer: County plat and deed records show the original Union Pacific grant pattern. We check this as part of every offer, since it directly affects royalty terms and closing paperwork.

faqs.question: My Goshen County minerals have never produced. Are they worth anything?
faqs.answer: Undeveloped Goshen County acreage is priced mainly on nearby lease bonus and permitting trends rather than an existing royalty stream, which is typical for this part of the basin. We can still make an offer on it.

faqs.question: Why does flank position matter for value?
faqs.answer: Well results near the edge of any chalk play vary more than they do in the thick core, so we weight actual nearby well performance more heavily than basin averages when pricing a flank-position tract.
